subject: [PATCH v7 1/6] fuse: decouple fuse_ring creation from ent registration

reviews.author: Baokun Li
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Baokun Li expressed concern that enabling capabilities beyond what was negotiated can introduce inconsistencies, referencing issues found in their downstream tree related to the fch->io_uring switch.

Reviewer Baokun Li noted that the current implementation of io_uring flags has unclear boundaries and inconsistent states, specifically mentioning enable_uring, fch->io_uring, and ring->ready. He suggested a clean design where fch->io_uring is set at INIT time based on negotiated flags and user-controlled enable_uring, and then write-once, with the io_uring path taken when ring->ready and falling back to classic /dev/fuse otherwise.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes, I saw it, but pre-existing doesn't necessarily mean correct.
Enabling capabilities beyond what was negotiated easily introduces
inconsistencies.

In our recent hardening work we found that the fch->io_uring switch
causes anomalies in several mechanisms (mostly in our downstream tree),
which is why I replied in Bernd's thread \u2014 he raised the
enable_uring / fch->io_uring bypass there.

---

Yes, that's exactly the problem. Right now we have several flags
with unclear boundaries:

 enable_uring: user-controlled, can be toggled at any time
 fch->io_uring: set to 1 at INIT negotiation, but cleared to 0
   on any entry registration failure \u2014 even if other entries
   have already registered successfully and fiq->ops has been
   switched to uring ops. The two states are inconsistent.
 ring->ready: set when at least one entry has registered

I think the clean design would be: at INIT time, decide based on
enable_uring and the negotiated flags whether to initialize uring
and set fch->io_uring. After that, enable_uring is no longer
consulted \u2014 fch->io_uring is write-once. When ring->ready (at
least one entry registered), take the io_uring path; otherwise
fall back to the classic /dev/fuse path. This way each
variable has a single, clear semantic.


Thanks,
Baokun

reviews.author: Baokun Li
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that a server skipping FUSE_OVER_IO_URING was never in a well-defined state due to lack of blocking guarantee and lock ordering protection, and agreed with the patch's decoupling approach.
reviews.raw_body:
Agreed. A server that skips FUSE_OVER_IO_URING was never in a
well-defined state \u2014 no blocking guarantee, no lock ordering
protection, nothing. There is nothing to preserve compatibility
with.


Thanks,
Baokun

reviews.author: Baokun Li
reviews.summary: The reviewer agrees that decoupling fuse_ring creation from ent registration is a good approach, as it simplifies the code structure by eliminating nested operations.
reviews.raw_body:
Makes sense \u2014 separating dequeue from send eliminates the nesting
structurally.


Cheers,
Baokun

2026-08-21.patch_summary: This patch decouples the creation of fuse_ring from entry registration in the FUSE (Filesystem in Userspace) driver. Currently, the ring is created lazily on the first FUSE_IO_URING_CMD_REGISTER command, which can lead to concurrent creations and requires open-coded handling. The patch moves the ring creation to the FUSE_INIT reply processing after a server has negotiated and set FUSE_OVER_IO_URING, ensuring that the ring is published before the connection is marked initialized. This change simplifies the code and reduces the risk of concurrent creations.
